title: Precision and output change the query cost
coverage: Bounded review of the two supplied statements from Mahabadi et al., with two explicitly identified full-scan baselines.

mahabadi-et-al-2026-matrix-mis-size.verificationVersion: Author manuscript arXiv:2510.11627v1; SODA 2026 publication confirmed by SIAM and author publication list

verifiedRecords.oracle: One query reveals whether the requested vertex pair is an edge
assumptions: General simple undirected graph
Only adjacency-matrix pair queries
MIS means inclusion-maximal, not maximum independent set
π is algorithm-generated; not a permutation fixed externally
No additive error
verifiedRecords.output: One scalar estimating an algorithm-generated random greedy MIS size
verifiedRecords.probability: High probability for correctness and running time; the proof uses parallel independent instances for the runtime guarantee
verifiedRecords.theorem: Theorem 1.3; Algorithm 4 and its following note; author manuscript printed pp. 3, 18–19
verifiedRecords.notes: The target is a generated permutation's greedy MIS size, not maximum independent set size or the expectation over permutations. The published time bound also bounds pair queries. The plotted segment uses the theorem where it improves on scanning.

verifiedRecords.oracle: One query reveals whether the requested vertex pair is an edge
assumptions: General simple undirected graph
Only adjacency-matrix pair queries
MIS means inclusion-maximal, not maximum independent set
Generate a permutation, read all unordered pairs, and execute greedy MIS
No claim to reproduce the amplified estimator's first-finishing permutation
verifiedRecords.quality: Exact size of the greedy MIS for its own generated π
verifiedRecords.probability: Always correct for the chosen permutation
verifiedRecords.theorem: Elementary full-scan derivation from the adjacency-matrix model and greedy MIS definition
verifiedRecords.notes: After at most n(n−1)/2 pair queries, greedy construction and counting use no further oracle queries. This baseline may choose its own π. Combining valid scalar-output algorithms gives the displayed query cap; this is an elementary derivation, not an additional theorem from the paper.

verifiedRecords.oracle: One query reveals whether the requested vertex pair is an edge
assumptions: General simple undirected graph
Only adjacency-matrix pair queries
MIS means inclusion-maximal, not maximum independent set
Read all unordered pairs, then run greedy in any fixed order
No ε approximation is required for explicit output
verifiedRecords.output: The full vertex set of one MIS
verifiedRecords.notes: The same complete matrix scan permits exact explicit construction. This is a direct baseline, not a new paper theorem. Its query order is independent of ε.

verifiedRecords.oracle: One query reveals whether the requested vertex pair is an edge
assumptions: General simple undirected graph
Only adjacency-matrix pair queries
MIS means inclusion-maximal, not maximum independent set
Explicit-output contract only
The hard input has a single edge at a random pair
Constant success probability bounded away from zero
verifiedRecords.output: The full vertex set of one MIS
verifiedRecords.probability: Worst-case query lower bound for constant-probability successful randomized construction; deterministic algorithms are included
verifiedRecords.notes: The source gives the hidden-edge construction obstruction. The pair-query interpretation follows the same search argument: a correct explicit MIS must exclude exactly one endpoint and include every other vertex. This does not lower-bound estimating its size; on that promised family the size is always n−1.

notes: No estimation lower bound is supplied or inferred.
Green marks algorithm upper bounds; red marks lower bounds. Setup color distinguishes the two output contracts.
The fixed ε=1/4 reference is illustrative and is now explicit, replacing the old unexplained x=1.25 point.
The raw theorem gives p=3/2+2a. The size panel displays the best available upper bound after adding the full-scan cap, min{3/2+2a,2}. This is an upper bound, not an optimality claim.
At exponent scale the scan cap starts at a=1/4; constants and logarithms can shift a finite-n crossover.
A generated π is not an external query and is not the expectation over permutations. The full-scan baseline may generate its own π.
Any fixed ε∈(0,1) has exponent 3/2; ε₀=1/4 is only the chosen reference. The displayed window a∈[0,1/2] samples polynomial precision regimes.
